results.question: How many PTO days do new employees get per year?
results.answer:
New full-time employees accrue **15 PTO days per year** during years 0–2.[Source: Pto Policy]  

Part-time employees also receive PTO, but it is accrued on a **pro-rated basis** rather than a fixed number of days.[Source: Pto Policy]

results.question: Can I carry over unused PTO days to next year?
results.answer: Yes. Employees may carry over **up to 5 unused PTO days** into the next calendar year, and any days above 5 are **forfeited on December 31**.[Source: Pto Policy]

results.question: Will I be paid out for unused PTO if I resign?
results.answer: Yes. The PTO policy says **accrued, unused PTO will be paid out upon voluntary resignation or termination**, up to a maximum of **10 days**.[Source: Pto Policy]

results.question: How many days per week do I need to be in the office?
results.answer: The **default hybrid schedule** requires employees to be on-site a minimum of **2 days per week**, typically **Tuesday and Thursday**, unless you and your manager agree otherwise.[Source: Remote Work Policy]

results.question: What is the home office equipment stipend?
results.answer:
The **home office equipment stipend** is a **one-time $500 stipend** for a home-office setup, available upon approval of a remote or hybrid arrangement. An **annual refresh stipend of $200** is available from **Year 2 onwards**.[Source: Remote Work Policy]

For related home office costs, the expense policy also allows **office supplies for a home office up to $100/year without prior approval** and a **work-from-home internet subsidy up to $50/month**.[Source: Expense Reimbursement Policy]
